prompts.prompt: design/ holds the full design package for our Report Export Service (system design, threat model, API, data model, IAM). It is about to be handed to the implementation team. Do the final design review and write design-review.md. Do not ask me questions; if something is unclear, state your assumption in the output and in your final message, and finish.
prompts.why_discriminating: The skill's quality gate defines exactly what blocks handoff (unmitigated HIGH threat, unhandled external dependency, access patterns without index support, breaking API change without versioning) and its scope rule says a 2-engineer, 5-req/min project should get simplicity-first feedback; an unguided review tends to list many issues at equal weight and may praise or ignore the 3-region active-active plus self-managed Kafka.

floor_checks.text: Findings ordered CRITICAL before IMPORTANT before SUGGESTION
floor_checks.check: python3 -c 'import re,sys;t=open("design-review.md").read();p=[m.start() for w in ("CRITICAL","IMPORTANT","SUGGESTION") for m in [re.search(w,t,re.I)] if m];sys.exit(0 if len(p)>=2 and p==sorted(p) else 1)'

rubric.criterion: Names the four quality-gate blockers as CRITICAL: T1 HIGH and unmitigated (GET /exports/{id} has no tenant check), MailRelay has no timeout/retry/fallback, data model cannot serve AP2/AP3 (no GSI), downloadUrl -> downloadUrls breaking change with no versioning
rubric.pass: All four, each tied to the file where it appears
rubric.partial: Two or three of the four
rubric.fail: One or none, or blockers mixed in with minor items at the same severity

rubric.criterion: Tailors to the small scope: calls 3-region active-active with global tables and EC2 Kafka over-engineering for ~300 requests/day and recommends removing or deferring them, with cost/operational reasoning
rubric.pass: Explicitly flags both as over-engineering for this load and says what to do instead
rubric.partial: Mentions one of them or hedges
rubric.fail: Accepts or recommends more scale features

rubric.criterion: Follows the skill's review structure: covers the ten areas (template adherence through actionable recommendations, including testability/CI-CD) and lists observability TBD, no runbook and unvalidated cost as IMPORTANT
rubric.pass: Ten areas addressed (briefly where not relevant) and the three IMPORTANT items present
rubric.partial: Most areas covered or IMPORTANT items partly present
rubric.fail: Unstructured list with no area coverage

rubric.criterion: Actionable fixes: tenant ownership check on GET /exports/{id}, MailRelay timeout + retry + DLQ/fallback, a GSI for tenant listing and stuck QUEUED jobs, /v2 or additive field for downloadUrls, scoped IAM instead of dynamodb:* on *, injectable clients for testing
rubric.pass: Concrete fixes for all blockers plus IAM and testability
rubric.partial: Fixes for blockers only, or generic

rubric.criterion: No false positives: does not call T2, T3 or T4 unmitigated (they have mitigations), does not invent services, numbers or requirements not in design/
rubric.pass: No false positives or invented facts
rubric.fail: Flags a mitigated threat as a blocker or invents facts

pairwise.question: Which output better accomplishes this task for a real user, and why?
focus: Are the true blockers separated from lesser issues?
Is the feedback right-sized for a 2-person, 5 req/min service?
Are the fixes concrete enough to act on before handoff?

prompts.prompt: Sprint 1 on the Report Export Service starts Monday. Write readiness.md with a go/no-go at the top. Do not ask me questions; if something is unclear, state your assumption in the output and in your final message, and finish.

prompts.prompt: Context change for the Report Export Service in design/: sales signed 40 enterprise tenants, so plan for about 2,000 export requests per minute at peak and a 99.95% availability target. The design docs are unchanged. Re-evaluate the design for this scope and write review-v2.md. Do not ask me questions; if something is unclear, state your assumption in the output and in your final message, and finish.
prompts.why_discriminating: The skill tailors feedback by project scope (small: avoid over-engineering; large: distributed reliability and failure resilience); a with-skill answer should change its stance on multi-region and decoupling while keeping the gate blockers, and look for scale bottlenecks (Lambda/stream concurrency, MailRelay throttling with no SLA, hot keys), whereas an unguided answer often repeats the small-scope review or rubber-stamps the existing multi-region plan.

rubric.criterion: Names the four quality-gate blockers as CRITICAL: T1 HIGH and unmitigated (GET /exports/{id} has no tenant check), MailRelay has no timeout/retry/fallback, data model cannot serve AP2/AP3 (no GSI), downloadUrl -> downloadUrls breaking change with no versioning
rubric.pass: All four, each tied to the file where it appears
rubric.partial: Two or three of the four
rubric.fail: One or none, or blockers mixed in with minor items at the same severity

rubric.criterion: Re-scopes: multi-region and a queue/stream are now justified or partly justified, with reasoning about what they buy at 99.95%; self-managed EC2 Kafka still questioned versus a managed option
rubric.pass: Explicitly revisits the earlier over-engineering stance with reasons
rubric.partial: Mentions scale but does not revisit multi-region/Kafka
rubric.fail: Still calls multi-region over-engineering, or accepts everything uncritically

rubric.criterion: Identifies scale bottlenecks: MailRelay throughput/throttling with no SLA, stream/Lambda concurrency, per-tenant hot keys or large Usage scans, the 10 req/min per-tenant usage plan versus 2,000/min
rubric.pass: At least three concrete bottlenecks with numbers from the prompt or design

rubric.criterion: Gives resilience measures matched to 99.95%: retries with backoff and DLQ, circuit breaker or queueing for MailRelay, alarms/SLOs, load and failure testing
rubric.pass: Specific measures tied to the availability target

rubric.criterion: No false positives: does not call T2, T3 or T4 unmitigated (they have mitigations), does not invent services, numbers or requirements not in design/
rubric.pass: No false positives or invented facts
rubric.fail: Flags a mitigated threat as a blocker or invents facts
